defaults.permitted_development: Across Cambridgeshire, hard surfacing is usually lowest risk on the planning permission route when drainage is handled properly, level changes stay modest and the work does not turn a soft frontage into a dominant engineered parking area. The route is usually strongest where the drainage story, frontage appearance and parking layout all work together rather than being solved separately.

rules.height_rules: Raised surfacing, retaining features and height or level changes can matter as much as the paving finish itself when councils assess hard-surface schemes in Cambridgeshire.
rules.depth_rules: Surface coverage, front garden drainage and overall project extent are usually the deciding issues for hard surfacing across Cambridgeshire, especially where large impermeable areas are proposed.
rules.boundary_rules: Frontage position, highway relationship and any linked access changes are often what make a hard-surfacing scheme more sensitive in Cambridgeshire.
rules.roof_rules: For hard-surface projects, the design equivalent of a roof check is usually the drainage fall and discharge strategy rather than any vertical structure.
rules.materials_rules: Permeable, visually restrained finishes are usually easier to justify than broad impermeable paving that removes planting and dominates the frontage.

rules.permitted_development: In Cambridge, hard surfacing is usually easiest to keep off the planning permission route where drainage is clear, levels stay sensible and the work does not turn the frontage into an over-engineered parking layout. The planning pressure often rises when the frontage starts to read more like engineered parking than simple domestic surfacing.

rules.height_rules: In Cambridge, even paving work can move into a closer review if it relies on raised height changes, retaining edges or platforms that materially change the site.
rules.depth_rules: Large impermeable areas in Cambridge usually deserve the earliest drainage check, particularly where the work affects the front garden or main parking area.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary treatment, highway relationship and crossover changes often shape the hard-surfacing answer in Cambridge more than the paving material alone.
rules.roof_rules: For hard surfacing in Cambridge, the key technical design question is usually where water goes and whether the falls avoid creating problems for neighbours or the highway.
rules.materials_rules: Permeable finishes and a softer overall frontage usually work better in Cambridge than extensive impermeable paving with little visual relief.

restrictions.conservation_area: Hard surfacing in conservation areas within Cambridge often faces a closer review where it changes the look of a visible frontage or removes established soft landscaping.
restrictions.listed_building: Works to the setting of a listed building in Cambridge, including resurfacing and level changes, can need a more careful planning and heritage review.
